family.name: one-factor Gaussian-copula conditional-independence closure 1FGC-8
family.dependence_information: one common latent Gaussian factor plus scalar marginals

inspected_closed_lanes.E039: two-component half-space Gaussian location mixture; distinct mechanism
inspected_closed_lanes.E124: Chow-Liu pairwise gate-amplitude tree; distinct mechanism
inspected_closed_lanes.E127: sparse higher-order Mobius hypergraph closure; distinct mechanism
inspected_closed_lanes.R215: coordinate-wise marginal characteristic functions only; no dependence carrier

primary_literature.citation: Krupskii P, Joe H. Factor copula models for multivariate data. Journal of Multivariate Analysis 120 (2013) 85-101.
primary_literature.claim_used: latent-factor conditional-independence copula representation with parsimonious O(d) dependence parameters

primary_literature.citation: Nataf A. Determination des distributions de probabilites dont les marges sont donnees. C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 255 (1962) 42-43.
primary_literature.claim_used: prescribed marginals combined with a normal dependence construction

exact_small.law_parity: uniform over four-Rademacher states with product +1
exact_small.one_factor_loading_implication: for Gaussian sign margins Corr(Xi,Xj)=2/pi*asin(lambda_i*lambda_j); pairwise independence gives lambda_i*lambda_j=0 for every i!=j, so at most one loading is nonzero and the modeled observed law is independent

terminal_reason: The family is cheap enough, but a single Gaussian latent factor cannot encode irreducible four-way parity dependence. The parity and independent laws have identical scalar marginals and identical pairwise laws, forcing the same 1FGC dependence state, yet the next dense ReLU mean differs by 1/4.
boundary_of_applicability: This result closes one-factor Gaussian-copula conditional-independence closure only. Multi-factor, vine, and explicit higher-order copula/state families are not covered and require new experiment identities.
